notes.pest_disease: Downy mildew is the primary disease concern, especially in humid conditions. Leaf miners can disfigure leaves. Choose resistant varieties and ensure good air circulation.
notes.harvest_marker: Harvest baby spinach at 3-4 inches. Full-size leaves at 5-7 inches. Harvest before plants bolt in warm weather.
notes.storage_handling: Store at 0 degrees C with very high humidity. Spinach is very perishable and should be sold within 5 days of harvest.
notes.cultivar_recommendation: Tyee is bolt-resistant and performs well across seasons. Corvair is excellent for baby leaf production. Bloomsdale is a classic savoy-type with excellent flavor.
notes.growing_tip: Spinach is a cool-season crop that struggles above 24 degrees C. Shade cloth extends production into early summer.
notes.irrigation: Consistent moisture promotes tender leaves. Overhead irrigation should be avoided in humid conditions to prevent disease.
